title: Otter Tail County receives state award for Empowered Worker Program
text:
Barry Fitzgibbons, Otter Tail County Sheriff | LinkedIn
Barry Fitzgibbons, Otter Tail County Sheriff | LinkedIn
Otter Tail County has announced that its Empowered Worker Program received the 2025 Outstanding Economic Development Award from the Minnesota Association of Professional County Economic Developers (MAPCED). The award was presented on December 9 during the Association of Minnesota Counties Annual Conference in Bloomington.
The Empowered Worker Program, started by Otter Tail County, aims to help individuals and families overcome barriers to employment and secure jobs that offer sustainable wages. Several county departments, including Community Development, Human Services, and Probation, work together on this initiative. Participants are provided with personalized support based on their individual goals and experiences. The program seeks to develop a workforce pipeline by connecting local talent with employers’ needs.
Nicole Hansen, Otter Tail County Administrator, said: “This recognition is a testament to the heart and innovation behind our Empowered Worker Program. We’re thrilled to see the work of our staff and community partners acknowledged at the state level.”
Wayne Johnson, Chair of the Otter Tail County Board, added: “This award means a lot to us. It’s proof that when you’ve got good folks working hard and motivated individuals wanting a better life for themselves, you can make real change. Our staff didn’t just follow a playbook. They built something that fits Otter Tail County, and now others are taking notice.”
Otter Tail County expressed gratitude to MAPCED and AMC for the honor and stated it remains committed to supporting residents through workforce initiatives. More information about the Empowered Worker Program is available at ottertailcounty.gov/otc-works.
Other updates from December include preparations for enhancements at Phelps Mill Park funded by grants; increased respiratory illness activity reported by healthcare providers ahead of the holiday season; an open house celebrating Perham’s new highway garage; upcoming meetings for January; volunteer opportunities for transporting clients through Human Services of Otter Tail and Wilkin Counties; scheduled flu shot clinics in Fergus Falls; and reminders about county office closures on New Year’s Day and Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
Board of Commissioners meetings can be re-watched online via YouTube or through links found on the Board of Commissioners page.
